source.title: Lookup-Table Recurrent Language Models for Long Tail Speech Recognition
source.authors: W. R. Huang; T. Sainath; Cal Peyser; Shankar Kumar; David Rybach; Trevor D. Strohman

record.tranche_reason: It measures held-out language-model log perplexity while varying the size and configuration of an n-gram embedding table, a different parameter-scaling setup from the original scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results for embedding-vocabulary scaling, n-gram order, and injection design. It also reports downstream WER. It does not test standard dense-model scaling across parameters, tokens, or compute, or fit small runs to predict much larger runs. Cited scaling-law results are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper (LookupLM). Its scaling results come from sweeping the size of its own sparse n-gram embedding table at fixed dense size. Embedding parameters are the kind the original laws exclude, and the sweep covers about 1.5 orders of magnitude. It does not test dense parameter, token or compute scaling of pretraining loss. The n-gram order and injection ablations are hyperparameters of the method, not depth or width shape at fixed parameter count. WER is the method's own downstream result, not a test of predictability from scale or loss. The authors' rough power-law remark is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that LookupLM improves log perplexity and long-tail WER with almost no extra dense compute. Their best model nearly matches a large dense LM that needs 6.2x the FLOPs. They also say reducing hash collisions by enlarging the table helps. The power-law remark is a brief aside in §4.2, not a main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Uses n-gram embedding lookup tables in an RNN language model; it does not reproduce the original dense-model parameter/token/compute scaling experiments or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Embedding vocabulary size changes performance; the paper also reports a tradeoff between embedding vocabulary and dimension, slight changes across n-gram order, no material difference from including the current token, and a slight performance reduction with first-layer-only injection.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed 22.2M dense parameters, scaling sparse n-gram embedding rows from 4k to 131k lowers log perplexity on all sets (e.g. RareALL 21.40 to 20.18). The authors say the relative gain 'roughly follows a power law', with exponent ~0.1 for linear perplexity and ~0.5 for WER. They see no saturation, but no fit is shown.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LM loss falls roughly as a power law in the number of sparse, lookup-only embedding parameters at fixed dense compute.

record.problems: The vocabulary sweep is limited to the reported LookupLM configurations; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper states that 131k was the limit when the 2048-dimensional table was stored on TPU. The reported downstream evaluation uses TTS audio, which the authors say they separately found correlated with recorded audio.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1c embedding-dimension/vocabulary tradeoff results, Table 1a baseline comparisons, Table 3 multidomain results, and Table 4 memory/FLOPs grid are not included because the 60-row cap was reached. Table 1c and Tables 3–4 are in sections 4.3, 4.7, and 4.6, respectively; Table 1a is in section 4.1.

untested.parts: Dense parameter, token and compute scaling of pretraining loss; not tested.
Depth and width at fixed parameter count.
Downstream performance versus scale or pretraining loss for standard models.

record.verdict_notes: The only dense-scaling evidence is a single comparison in Table 1a. Going from B1 (5.5M dense) to B2 (59.5M dense) lowers Head log perplexity from 7.09 to 6.70. Two points cannot test power-law form. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The reader's three 'supports' labels are withdrawn.

versions.untested_parts: Tests log perplexity while scaling LookupLM embedding-table vocabulary over the reported range; does not test token-count or compute scaling, standard dense-parameter scaling, or scaling over several orders of magnitude.
Tests n-gram order and injection design; does not provide a broad comparison of depth and width at fixed parameter count.
Tests WER on the reported speech-recognition sets; does not test predictability across a range of downstream tasks or relate downstream performance systematically to pretraining loss.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LookupLM embedding vocabulary sweep, 4k to 131k, on Head, RareASR, and RareALL
reader_labels.reason: Log perplexity falls across the sweep, and the authors report that relative gain in this range roughly follows a power law (rows r01–r18). This is limited to the tested embedding-table setting and range.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: tested n-gram orders and injection/context variations
reader_labels.reason: The authors report slight variation across n-gram orders 2–6, little effect from shifting the context to include the current token, and a slight loss when using first-layer-only injection (rows r19–r39).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: WER across the embedding-vocabulary sweep on the reported speech-recognition sets
reader_labels.reason: RareASR and RareALL WER improve as vocabulary grows, and Head WER is broadly similar or somewhat lower, with a small increase at 8k (rows r40–r57).
